extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of Euclid's Elements; learners of classical Euclidean geometry
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of Book III (circles) propositions and constructions from Euclid's Elements, including theorem statements and their constructive/proof guidance. Covers properties of circles, tangents, equal segments/circumferences, and related constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point-within-circle-with-more-than-two-equal-lines-is-centre (Prop. IX)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a point be taken within a circle, from which there fall more than two equal straight lines to the circumference, that point is the centre of the circle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement: given D inside circle ABC with DA = DB = DC, then D is the centre. Proof outline: assume another centre E, draw DE and produce to meet circumference at F,G so FG is a diameter; then distances from D to circumference along FG would vary, giving a contradiction to equality of DA, DB, DC; conclude D is the unique centre. (Uses contradiction via largest distance from an off-centre point to circumference.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Two_circumferences_cannot_cut_in_more_than_two_points (Prop. X)
rubrics_metrics.description: One circumference of a circle cannot cut another in more than two points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement: If circumferences FAB and DEF met in B,G,F (three points), then the centre K of ABC would be inside DEF and equidistant to more than two points KB,KG, KF, implying K is also the centre of DEF, i.e. the same centre for two distinct circles that cut, which is impossible. Thus two circles meet in at most two points. (Uses previous proposition: point with >2 equal lines is centre.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Line_through_centres_of_internally_tangent_circles_passes_through_point_of_contact (Prop. XI/XL)
rubrics_metrics.description: If two circles touch each other internally, the straight line which joins their centres being produced shall pass through the point of contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement: circles ABC and ADE touch internally at A; centres F and G: line FG produced passes through A. Proof outline: assume FG does not pass through A, construct perpendiculars/segments and compare lengths to reach contradiction (comparing remainders after subtracting common part FG). Conclude FG must pass through the contact point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line_through_centres_of_externally_tangent_circles_passes_through_point_of_contact (Prop. XII)
rubrics_metrics.description: If two circles touch each other externally, the straight line which joins their centres shall pass through the point of contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement: circles ABC and ADE touch externally at A; centres F and G: line FG passes through A. Proof outline: assume otherwise, show sums/inequalities of radii and parts lead to contradiction (FG both greater and less than sum of AF and AG), concluding FG must pass through A.

rubrics_metrics.name: A_circle_cannot_touch_another_in_more_than_one_point (Prop. XIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: One circle cannot touch another in more points than one, whether it touches it on the inside or outside.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof split: interior case — if EBF touched ABC in B and D, joining BD and bisecting at right angles gives centre-line GH which cannot pass through the point of contact as required, contradiction. Exterior case — if ACK touched ABC at A and C, join AC: AC would be simultaneously within and without one circle, contradiction. Therefore only one contact point is possible in each internal/external case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal_lines_in_circle_are_equally_distant_from_centre_and_converse (Prop. XIV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Equal straight lines in a circle are equally distant from the centre; and those which are equally distant from the centre, are equal to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: from centre E draw perpendiculars EF, EG to equal chords AB, CD. Show EF = EG by comparing halves and using right-angle square relations: AF = CG leads to EF = EG. Converse: if perpendiculars from centre to two chords are equal, corresponding chord halves are equal, hence chords equal. (Uses perpendicular from centre bisects chord and Pythagorean relations.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Diameter_is_greatest_and_nearness_to_centre_ranks_line_lengths (Prop. XV)
rubrics_metrics.description: The diameter is the greatest straight line in a circle; and, of all others, that which is nearer to the centre is always greater than one more remote; and the greater is nearer to the centre than the less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: diameter AD is longer than any non-diameter BC by comparing EB,EC relative to arc and applying previous results; if BC nearer to centre than FG then BC > FG (construct perpendiculars from centre and compare halves and squares). Converse likewise: greater chord is nearer centre. (Uses preceding proposition on perpendiculars to chords and square comparisons.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Perpendicular_to_diameter_from_extremity_falls_without_circle_and_no_line_between_it_and_circumference_avoids_circle (Prop. XVI)
rubrics_metrics.description: The straight line drawn at right angles to the diameter of a circle, from the extremity of it, falls without the circle; and no straight line can be drawn between that straight line and the circumference from the extremity so as not to cut the circle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement: from extremity A of diameter AB draw AE perpendicular to AB; AE lies outside circle. Proof: assume it met circle then produce contradiction by right-angle properties. Also show any line between AE and circumference from A must cut the circle: suppose FA between them and draw DG ⟂ FA to reach contradiction (DH > DG etc.). Corollary: AE is a tangent at A and unique tangent at that point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct_tangent_from_given_point_outside_or_on_circumference (Prop. XVII)
rubrics_metrics.description: To draw a straight line from a given point, either without or in the circumference, which shall touch a given circle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: For external point A: find centre E, join AE, describe circle AFG centred at E with radius EA, draw DF ⟂ EA from point D where small circle meets given circle, join EB, AB is tangent. Proof uses congruent triangles AEB and FED showing EBA is right angle, hence AB tangent. For point on circumference D: draw DE to centre, then DF ⟂ DE is the tangent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radius_to_point_of_contact_is_perpendicular_to_tangent (Prop. XVIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a straight line touches a circle, the straight line drawn from the centre to the point of contact shall be perpendicular to the line touching the circle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement: DE touches circle ABC at C; joining FC (centre to contact) yields FC ⟂ DE. Proof: assume some other perpendicular from F meets DE at G; compare FC and FG using opposite-angle/greatest-side arguments and equal radii contradictions to conclude FC must be perpendicular and unique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centre_lies_on_line_at_right_angles_to_tangent_from_point_of_contact (Prop. XIX)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a straight line touches a circle, and from the point of contact a straight line be drawn at right angles to the touching line, the centre of the circle shall be in that line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement: DE tangent at C, draw CA ⟂ DE; centre lies on CA. Proof: assume centre F not on CA then FC ⟂ DE (from previous prop) giving two right angles at C leading to contradiction of inequality of angles; so centre must lie on CA. (Uniqueness argument.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Angle_at_centre_double_of_angle_at_circumference_on_same_base (Prop. XX)
rubrics_metrics.description: The angle at the centre of a circle is double of the angle at the circumference, upon the same base, that is, upon the same part of the circumference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider cases: centre inside or outside the angle at circumference. Join centre E to vertices and produce one radius where necessary. Use isosceles triangles (equal radii) to show centre-angle equals sum/double of corresponding inscribed angles; conclude central angle BEC = 2 × inscribed angle BAC. (Standard Euclidean proof splitting into cases.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Angles_in_same_segment_are_equal (Prop. XXI)
rubrics_metrics.description: The angles in the same segment of a circle are equal to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let BAD and BED be angles in same segment BAED. Take centre F and use proposition that central angle is double inscribed angle: compare relevant centre angles to deduce equality of inscribed angles. If segment ≤ semicircle, extend diameter and reduce to previous case. (Uses Prop. XX.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposite_angles_of_cyclic_quadrilateral_sum_to_two_right_angles (Prop. XXII)
rubrics_metrics.description: The opposite angles of any quadrilateral figure described in a circle are together equal to two right angles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Join diagonals AC, BD. Use that triangle angles sum to two right angles and that opposite angles subtend same arcs (angles in same segment). Combine equalities to show sum of opposite angles equals two right angles. (Standard cyclic quadrilateral property.)

rubrics_metrics.name: No_two_similar_segments_on_same_side_of_line_without_coinciding (Prop. XXIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon the same straight line, and upon the same side of it, there cannot be two similar segments of circles not coinciding with one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume two similar segments ACB and ADB lie on same side of AB and do not coincide; one must lie within the other. Draw connecting lines and use that similar segments contain equal angles, producing an exterior/interior angle equality contradiction. Hence they must coincide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Similar_segments_on_equal_lines_are_equal (Prop. XXIV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Similar segments of circles upon equal straight lines are equal to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If segments AEB and CFD are similar on equal straight lines AB and CD, apply AEB to CFD aligning endpoints; because AB = CD the endpoints coincide and hence the segments coincide and are equal. (Simple congruence/placement argument.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct_circle_from_given_segment (Prop. XXV)
rubrics_metrics.description: A segment of a circle being given, to describe the circle of which it is the segment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: Bisect chord AC at D; draw DB ⟂ AC and join AB. If angles ABD and BAD equal then D is centre; else at A make angle BAE equal ABD, produce BD to E, join EC. Show AE = EB and AD = DC and DE common so E equidistant AE=EB=EC; E is centre. Describe circle from E with radius EA. Notes: location of centre relative to segment (within/on/without) determines whether segment is >, =, or < semicircle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal_angles_in_equal_circles_stand_on_equal_circumferences (Prop. XXVI)
rubrics_metrics.description: In equal circles, equal angles stand upon equal circumferences, whether they be at the centres or circumferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given equal circles ABC and DEF with equal centre angles and equal inscribed angles, join corresponding chord bases BC and EF. Equal radii make corresponding isosceles triangles equal, so bases BC = EF; similar segments on equal lines are equal, hence the circumferences subtended by equal angles are equal. (Uses previous propositions about segments and equal chords.)

rubrics_metrics.name: In_equal_circles_angles_on_equal_circumferences_are_equal (Prop. XXVII)
rubrics_metrics.description: In equal circles, the angles which stand upon equal circumferences are equal to one another, whether they be at the centres or circumferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If circumferences BC and EF are equal in equal circles ABC and DEF, then central angles BGC and EHF are equal; otherwise produce an angle equal to one and reach contradiction by comparing circumferences (less to greater). Inscribed angles are halves of central angles, hence equal too.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal_straight_lines_in_equal_circles_cut_off_equal_circumferences (Prop. XXVIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: In equal circles, equal straight lines cut off equal circumferences, the greater equal to the greater, and the less to the less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let equal circles ABC, DEF have equal chords BC and EF which cut off greater circumferences BAC and EDF and lesser BGC and EHF. Using equal radii BK-KC = EL-LF and base equality show central angles equal, hence equal circumferences of corresponding greater/lesser arcs. Then the complementary arcs equal as whole circles equal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal_circumferences_in_equal_circles_subtend_equal_lines (Prop. XXIX)
rubrics_metrics.description: In equal circles, equal circumferences are subtended by equal straight lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given equal circumferences BGC and EHF in equal circles ABC and DEF, join BC and EF and let centres K,L. Equal circumferences imply equal central angles BKC and ELF; equal radii plus equal contained angles imply bases BC = EF. (Direct converse of previous props.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Bisect_a_circumference (Prop. XXX)
rubrics_metrics.description: To bisect a given circumference, that is, to divide it into two equal parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: join chord AB of given arc ADB, bisect AB at C, draw CD ⟂ AB, join AD and DB. Using congruent triangles ACD and BCD (AC=CB, CD common, right angles) show AD = DB; equal chords cut equal circumferences, so circumference ADB bisected at D. (Uses chord bisection and perpendicular from centre.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Angle_in_semicircle_and_segments_relation (Prop. XXXI)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a circle, the angle in a semicircle is a right angle; but the angle in a segment greater than a semicircle is less than a right angle; and the angle in a segment less than a semicircle is greater than a right angle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: For diameter BC and point A on circle, join AE to centre E and produce BA. From equal radii derive angle BAC equals exterior angle FAC, showing it a right angle. For segment greater than semicircle, triangle relations show angle is less than right; for segment less than semicircle, opposite angle in cyclic quadrilateral is greater than right. Corollary: if one angle of triangle equals sum of the other two then it is a right angle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tangent-chord_angle_equals_angle_in_alternate_segment (Prop. XXXII)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a straight line touches a circle, and from the point of contact a straight line be drawn cutting the circle, the angles made by this line with the line touching the circle, shall be equal to the angles which are in the alternate segments of the circle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Setup: EF touches circle ABCD at B; BD cuts circle. Draw BA ⟂ EF to locate centre on BA and pick C on arc BD. Use right-angle at semicircle and equalities of triangle angles to show DBF (angle between chord and tangent) equals inscribed angle BAD in alternate segment; similarly DBE equals angle BCD. Uses Prop. XVI, XVIII, XXI, XXII.
